source.title: What Can Grokking Teach Us About Learning Under Nonstationarity?
source.authors: Clare Lyle; Ghada Sokar; Razvan Pascanu; András Gyorgy

record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for a randomly initialized transformer on modular arithmetic, a new task setting for the broader claim.
record.gate_note: The paper says training accuracy is not plotted and reports only an aggregate statement: almost all networks reach perfect or near-perfect accuracy quickly, with unspecified exceptions. Its CIFAR-10 results report test accuracy, not training classification error. Other results concern generalization, feature learning, or reinforcement-learning returns. The paper cites prior work on learning-rate and stability dynamics, but does not test the specific stability-limit claims in V5.
record.test_reason: No results test V1–V6 as stated. R1 measures transformer training accuracy on modular arithmetic, outside V1's convolutional-network and CIFAR setting. The other experiments measure generalization, feature changes, or RL returns. References to catapult and edge-of-stability dynamics motivate learning-rate re-warming but provide no stability-threshold, curvature, or training-loss test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that effective-learning-rate re-warming can induce feature learning, accelerate grokking, close warm-starting generalization gaps, and improve high-UTD RL performance. They emphasize parameter-norm control and careful annealing, particularly in RL, to avoid instability.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a transformer on modular arithmetic and reports training accuracy; the claim versions concern other tasks, architectures, interventions, or outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: For the reported training-accuracy finding, the paper states that nearly all networks reach perfect or near-perfect accuracy quickly; it does not break this result down by condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Almost all modular-arithmetic transformers attain perfect or near-perfect training accuracy, typically within one thousand steps; training accuracy is not plotted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformers trained with Adam on this modular-arithmetic task can rapidly attain near-perfect training accuracy across most tested configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective-learning-rate re-warming facilitates feature changes and generalization in grokking and warm-started CIFAR-10 classification; high-UTD RL benefits require subsequent annealing to control instability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transient effective-learning-rate increases can facilitate feature replacement and improve generalization or RL returns, depending on parameter-norm control, architecture, and annealing.

record.peer_reviewed: Published at 4th Conference on Lifelong Learning Agents (CoLLAs), 2025
record.problems: Training accuracy is not plotted; the result is an aggregate qualitative statement with no count of networks, identified exceptions, or uncertainty estimate.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were retained: CIFAR-10 warm-starting plots report test accuracy and feature metrics, while reinforcement-learning results report returns; neither measures training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error of sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and model-size, stopping, or regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems as teacher width and excess student width vary.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts, special plain-network initialization, or Fixup.
Effects of activation-matched initialization and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, accompanying loss and curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, and threshold-related divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons measuring training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked R1 and its assessment that all six versions are untested. LayerNorm and projection experiments concern generalization rather than V6's batch-normalization training-speed comparison. Appendix C analyzes feature evolution under simplified updates rather than any listed claim.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; size, early-stopping, and regularization conditions described in the version.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks at increasing depth; special initialization and residual normalization conditions.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep plain networks.
Stability-limit sweeps, loss and curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability sharpness, and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: transformer with a single attention block
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; trained on the task
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modular arithmetic task; training accuracy was not plotted.
rows.value: Almost all networks attain perfect or near-perfect training accuracy almost immediately after training begins (typically within one thousand steps).
rows.note: Aggregate result; the text does not give the number of networks or identify the exceptions.
rows.check: The qualitative training-accuracy statement is accurately extracted, but it cannot establish any listed version. Its original observed state describes the modular-arithmetic finding only. The aggregate statement does not identify exceptions or separate normalization, projection, learning-rate, and weight-decay conditions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
